definitions.explanation: The initial starting point. Most commonly used in the expression 振り出しに戻る (to go back to square one), referring to returning to the beginning after progress is lost.

examples.japanese: {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}ってしまった。
examples.english: We ended up back at square one.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}が{決裂|けつれつ}して、すべてが{振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}った。
examples.english: Negotiations broke down and everything went back to square one.

examples.japanese: データが{消|き}えて、{一|いち}から{振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}ってやり{直|なお}すしかない。
examples.english: The data was lost, so there's no choice but to go back to the beginning and start over from scratch.

notes:
USAGE:
{振|ふ}り{出|だ}し originally refers to the starting square in a board game (like sugoroku). The expression {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}る (to go back to square one) is extremely common and is the primary way this word is used in everyday Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}る (to go back to square one)
- {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しから (from the beginning)
- {振|ふ}り{出|だ}しに{戻|もど}す (to put something back to the starting point)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The word comes from すごろく (Japanese backgammon/board game), where {振|ふ}り{出|だ}し is the starting square. Landing on certain squares sends you back to {振|ふ}り{出|だ}し.
